subject: anyone know of a function to identify node numbers by phylogenetic definition?

messages.author: 3767d2380f73cdd8
messages.subject: anyone know of a function to identify node numbers by phylogenetic definition?
parts:
I'm trying to run Biogeobears over a bunch of trees that vary in topology and branch length (a set of likely trees from a bayesian analysis with many fossil tips). In order to summarize the results at particular nodes, I need to be able to identify the correct node numbers for particular clades, but I can't do that by using the mrca functions because the clade content is variable and the changes in topology change the node numbers.  I need to identify the most inclusive clade containing taxa X and Y, but not taxon Z. If anyone has experienced a similar problem or knows of r functions that might be able to help I'd love to hear them!

Joey

messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] anyone know of a function to identify node numbers by phylogenetic definition?
parts:
Hi Joey!

I have some code for this but it's not in the package yet.  But if you have some R skillz it's not too hard.  A handy function that is in BioGeoBEARS is 
prt():

tr = read.tree(file="whatever.newick")
prt(tr)

...this converts a tree to a much handier table format.

If you do:

===============================
tr_table = prt(tr, printflag=FALSE, get_tipnames=TRUE)
tr_table
===============================

...then this column:

tr_table$tipnames

...will have, for each node in the tree, a string with the alphabetical, comma-delimited list of species descending from that node.

Since each list is alphabetical, you can just match strings to match nodes between two trees...

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] anyone know of a function to identify node numbers by phylogenetic definition?
parts:
Awesome! prt is very helpful. Here is what I came up with, operating on the knowledge that the lowest numbered node that contains two taxa of interest should always have the most total taxa.

mostinclusive() returns the node number of the most inclusive clade containing taxon1 and taxon2, but not taxon3. taxon names should be in quotes when calling the function, e.g. mostinclusive(tree,"taxon1","taxon2","taxon3")

mostinclusive <- function(tree,taxon1, taxon2, taxon3){
tr_table = prt(tree, printflag=FALSE, get_tipnames=TRUE)
taxon1matches=grep(taxon1,tr_table$tipnames)
taxon2matches=grep(taxon2,tr_table$tipnames)
taxon3matches=grep(taxon3,tr_table$tipnames)
commonclades=intersect(taxon1matches,taxon2matches)
removetaxon3=setdiff(commonclades,taxon3matches)
inclusive=min(removetaxon3)
return(inclusive)
}

Thanks again,
Joey
